messages.author: e9c08dbaa40beb96
messages.subject: ctmm.select - Error in if (!verbose && any(BAD)) { :    missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
parts:
Hi all, 

I have segregated 5 months of irregularly-sampled bird relocation data based on diel period (day/night), and behaviour (accelerometry) (high and low activity fixes). The DT plot and variogram for 1 individual (UUR Night Low) are below. 






Running ctmm models for all individuals worked, except for one individual (UUR night low). I used the following code: 

uur.night.low <- tele_list$`Night.Low Activity`$UUR
PROTO.12h <- ctmm(
  mean = "periodic",
  period = c(12 %#% "hours"),
  error = FALSE
)
guess.uur.nl <- ctmm.guess(uur.night.low, CTMM = PROTO.12h, interactive = F)

I got the following response: 

> fit.uur.nl <- ctmm.select(uur.night.low, CTMM = guess.uur.nl, verbose = T, trace = T) Nyquist frequency estimated at harmonic 6 of the period. * Fitting model OUF anisotropic harmonic 0 Nyquist of the period. * Fitting model IID anisotropic harmonic 3 Nyquist frequency estimated at harmonic 5.99779951065665 of the period. * Fitting model OU harmonic 3
Error in if (!verbose && any(BAD)) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages: 1: In omega * t : longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length 2: In omega * t : longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

I am wondering if anyone else has had the same error message? I am thinking that the 12-hourly periodic model may struggle when there are extended temporal gaps.  However, it did not pose any problems for the other individuals with the same temporal gaps. 

Cheers, 
Alex
